newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish MPs pass bill on PAP news agency sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Polish MPs pass bill on PAP news agency sell-off.

text.p: Poland's lower house of Parliament, the Sejm, passed a bill on Thursday to pave the way to sell national press agency PAP after it is transformed into a treasury-owned joint stock company.

By a vote of 368 to 11 with three abstentions, the Sejm said it expected to sell up to 49 percent of the news agency in two years, after it becomes a joint-stock firm. PAP said it expects to be a joint-stock firm at the start of 1998.
PAP will be managed in line with the commerical code, except that its first president and board will be chosen by the Treasury minister and approved by the prime minister.
The bill, now sent to the Senate, also envisions creating an advisory programme board whose specific functions would later be set in the new PAP statute.
PAP said its character would be "of a public press agency, which among other things, is obliged to publicise the stance of Poland's Sejm, Senate, President and government."
The government will subsidise PAP until it is partially privatised, it said.
